head: pr17457-r10
report:
Running the four key prior probes against this head in parallel.

NO DEFECTS

## NOT A DEFECT

I copied the prior round's probes into scratch without editing their bytes. Relative helper imports resolve through symlinks to the original `/mnt/nvme/tmp-omp-batch` helper directories, and `REVIEW_ROOT` points at this head. On the first run all four files failed for an environment reason: `REVIEW_ARTIFACTS` was unset, so the helper's `note()` threw on `undefined/results.jsonl`. The results below come from a second run with `REVIEW_ARTIFACTS` set.

**Prior findings: are they closed at this head?**

- **P1, Mnemopi recall/reflect embeddings after cancellation: closed.**
  - `mnemopi-embedding.test.ts` passes all three live controls. Each sends one request to `/embeddings` with `Bearer review-embed-key`.
  - The three disposal/cancel cases (`recall`, `reflect`, `recallForContext`) time out at 15 s. The probe waits at `await received.promise`, which resolves only when the endpoint receives a request. A timeout therefore means no embedding request arrived in 15 s after `beginDispose()` plus caller abort, with the credential already released.
  - The prior round saw one disposed request in each of these cases.

- **P1, startup skill compression captured no session lifetime: closed.**
  - `skill-sdk.test.ts`: the live control receives `[{disposed:false, credential:"sk-local-test"}]`.
  - The `beginDispose()` case times out at 20 s waiting on the same "request received" promise, so no request was sent. The prior round saw `[true]`.

- **P1, seven subagent opt-outs kept sending provider requests during disposal: closed.**
  - `survivesBeginDispose` jobs now run inside `runInRequestHoldScope` (`job-manager.ts`). `withRequestHold` (`stream.ts`) and `withAuth` (`auth-retry.ts`) check the hold when a request starts and again after its credential resolves.
  - `optout-window.test.ts`, credentialed requests per opted-out job after disposal begins:

    | Mode | Prior round | This head |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `immediate` | 0 | 0 |
    | `one-shutdown-handler` | 87–88 | 1 each, all 4.1–5.9 ms after start |
    | `three-shutdown-handlers` | 113–114 | 0 |
    | `beginDispose-gap` | 55–56 | 1 for two sites (≈2.0 ms), 0 for the rest |

    The non-opted control is 0 in every mode.
  - The single early requests show up only in some runs and only within the first few milliseconds. They are requests whose `stream()` call had already passed admission before the hold engaged, which `request-hold.ts` documents ("A request already sent before the hold runs to completion"). No job made a second request.
  - The probe's own assertion `>0` fails only because it was written to measure the old leak.

- **P2, Sharpshooter extraction paid for output it could not keep: closed.**
  - `exceptions.test.ts`:

    | Case | Requests | Deltas persisted |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | live | 1 | 1 |
    | after `beginDispose()` | 1 | 1 (the reply is now kept) |
    | after `dispose()` resolves | 0 | 0 (the request is no longer sent) |

  - The single failure (expected one request after full disposal) is the old probe's retention expectation. The prior round asked for either a flush that keeps its answer or cancellation; the extraction now does both, at the right points.

- **`/annotate` exception: closed in source.**
  - The old probe calls `generateTextReviewContextSummary` with no signal, so it still records `[true]`; it does not go through the fixed path.
  - In this head, `runAnnotateCommand` passes `ctx.signal`. The only `CustomCommandContext` builder (`agent-session.ts:9334`) sets `signal: this.#disposeAbortController.signal`, so the signal does reach the consumer.

- **P2, ownership checker was only an inventory: addressed.**
  - The walk now covers 12 packages and 339 sites, including the transports in `packages/ai`, `packages/agent` and `packages/catalog`.
  - `test/model-request-ownership.test.ts` and `test/async-job-manager.test.ts` pass 44/0; `packages/ai/test/request-hold.test.ts` passes 8/0.
  - I did not re-run the prior round's 14 checker attacks. Their harness relocates the source root, which is outside this budget.

**Suspicions ruled out**

- **Wrapping the resolver key changes its identity.** In `withRequestHold`, `holdAfterKeyResolution` replaces a resolver `apiKey` with a wrapper. `isApiKeyResolver` only checks `typeof key === "function"` and `ApiKeyResolver` is a plain function type, so no marker or property is lost.
- **Hold scope leaking into completion handling.** The hold scope wraps only the job body. The job's completion, delivery and eviction code runs after an `await` in the outer context, so it is not held.
- **Remote compaction bypassing the hold — not asserted.** `requestOpenAiRemoteCompaction` / `requestRemoteCompaction` (`packages/agent`) call `fetch` directly, not through `stream` or `withAuth`, so a held subagent that hits context overflow on an in-flight reply could in principle send one. `docs/sdk.md` explicitly limits the hold to pi-ai's `stream`, `streamSimple`, `complete*` and `withAuth`, and I did not reproduce this. It is unproven and outside the stated contract, so I am not reporting it as a defect.
